subject: Physical data paths, GPU-fencing & archival strategy for on-prem K8s preflight

Subject: Planning: physical data paths, GPU fencing, and archival strategy for on-prem cluster

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this on. We're planning a private deployment for a regulated customer (EdgeHost client) and want to lock down the physical and logical data paths before the preflight. A few items we want your guidance on:

- GPU fencing / tenant isolation: customer wants strong hardware-level isolation between inference tenants and non-critical batch workloads. They prefer node-level fencing but are open to PCIe partitioning if needed.
- Storage tiers: local NVMe for cache/hot-models, a resilient replicated tier for model artifacts, and a low-cost archival tier for older checkpoints.
- Network flows: separation of management plane traffic from inference data, and egress rules for telemetry to Redwood's control plane (they want minimal outbound).
- Evacuation plan: how to drain GPU nodes without losing pinned model state or corrupting cache layers.

Attached is our latest rack layout (rack-layout-v3.pdf) and an NVMe bay sketch (nvme-layout.png). Can your team propose a concise node-pool / PV strategy and a short checklist we can include in the customer's runbook?

Best,
Roberto
Ops Lead, EdgeHost
EdgeHost Infrastructure
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Planning: physical data paths, GPU fencing, and archival strategy for on-prem cluster

Roberto —

Appreciate the attachments and clear list. High level responses and proposed actions below; Marissa and Dylan will add sizing and operational runbook details.

1) GPU fencing / isolation
- Preferred approach: dedicate "inference-gpu" nodepool(s) with hardware affinity to isolated racks/PCIe fabrics. Use taints + tolerations to restrict inference pods; RBAC network policies to prevent lateral tenant access.
- If the customer needs absolute HW partitioning, we can evaluate SR-IOV or MIG (if using Ampere/ARM or NVIDIA A100/A30 with MIG profiles). Note: MIG reduces per-GPU capacity for very fine isolation.

2) Storage tiering
- Hot: local NVMe on inference nodes for KV cache and model shard read-paths (fast ephemeral cache).
- Warm: replicated block store (Ceph/Rook or SAN-backed PVCs) for model artifacts that must survive node reboots. We'll prefer Read-Through cache pattern to minimize warm-tier writes.
- Cold/Archive: object storage (S3-compatible) on a rink with lifecycle rules; encrypted-at-rest and immutable retention as required.

3) Network and control plane flows
- Require separate VLANs or VRFs for management (kube-apiserver, etcd, node management) and inference data plane.
- Minimal outbound: we can limit control-plane egress to a small set of Redwood endpoints and use a relay (customer-managed) to reduce exposure.

4) Evacuation and state preservation
- For pinned models: prefer pushing model artifacts to warm-tier before evacuation; adopt coordinated drain hook that uploads final cache delta to warm-tier/object-store snapshot.
- For long-running KV caches: use TTLs and rehydration strategy — document expected warmup time and SLO degradation windows.

Action items (short):
- Marissa: provide nodepool definitions, taints/tolerations, and PV classes.
- Dylan: propose migration/drain hooks and a sample evacuation playbook.
- I'll assemble a one-page preflight checklist and share a draft.

Deliverable timeline: draft checklist & nodepool proposal by EOD today; full runbook by end of week.

Vivek

Subject: Re: Planning: physical data paths, GPU fencing, and archival strategy for on-prem cluster

Quick proposals to slot into the checklist — keeping the runbook minimal and testable:

Nodepools (example)
- inference-gpu-prod: 4x A100-40GB per rack, taint: inference=true:NoSchedule, tolerations only for inference service accounts, PV class: local-nvme-fast
- inference-gpu-burst: identical hardware but in separate rack and tagged for preemptible workloads; used for tenant burst with lower QoS
- batch-gpu: for non-customer workloads, completely isolated racks, different kubelet config and no access to inference PVs
- control-plane: dedicated masters (3x) on separate VLAN with isolated etcd storage on resilient SAN

PV strategy
- local-nvme-fast: HostPath/Local PVs with CSI driver for NVMe; mountPropagation disabled for safety. Use as cache only (not source-of-truth).
- replicated-block: Rook-Ceph RBD backed PVCs for model artifacts and checkpoints; replication factor 3 recommended for rack-level failure tolerance.
- archive-sync: cronjob-based sync to S3-compatible gateway with retention tags.

Evacuation flow (short)
1. Mark node Unschedulable; 2. Trigger model push to replicated-block for pinned artifacts; 3. Drain with a special drain-script that waits for cache-flush hook (max 10 min) and captures logs to a central store; 4. Verify model checksums post-schedule.

Notes on NVMe layout (see nvme-layout.png):
- Keep PCIe lanes dedicated to GPU hosts to avoid NUMA interference.
- Avoid mixing inference NVMe with local system volumes — use separate controllers if possible.

I'm attaching a one-page CSV inventory for rack/bay mapping and will drop a short checklist (preflight-checklist.xlsx) to your Drive link.

-marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
